data.name: Nabarun
data.gender_notes: Nabarun is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nabarun is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Nabha' (night) and 'Runa' (runner). This name is associated with the Hindu deity Krishna, who is often depicted as the 'Nabhavasanta Raja' (King of the Night). The name Nabarun carries the meaning “Night Runner” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nabarun usually hope their child will grow to embody night runner and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes courage and protection in the darkness of life.
data.etymology: Nabarun belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night Runner.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nabarun total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nabarun carries a rich cultural significance in Hinduism. It is a unique and intriguing name that reflects the deep connection Hindus have with the natural world and the cycles of day and night. The name resonates with the rhythm of the universe and is often used to honor the eternal cycle of life and death.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Nabarun is a reminder of the transient nature of life and the infinite wisdom and protection of Krishna, the god of love, compassion, and preservation. It is believed that invoking the name of Krishna, the 'Nabhavasanta Raja', provides comfort, strength, and guidance during difficult times, and helps to keep the mind focused on the divine. We can strive to emulate the qualities of Krishna's divine nature by living in harmony with the natural world and treating all beings with love and compassion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nabarun symbolizes the constant cycle of renewal and rebirth, represented by the nine planets (Navagrahas) and the cyclic flow of the sun (Ravi). It embodies the spirit of overcoming challenges and moving forward with each new beginning.

historical_references.reference: In Bengali literature, Nabarun is a pen name of renowned writer Atish Dipankar Tasar; he was born on 1 March 1940 in the village of Ranagarh, in the Birbhum district of West Bengal, India.

Another Nabarun, known as Nababharat Sena, was a Mughal military commander during the late 16th century. He was a trusted general of Akbar and played a significant role in the Battle of Haldighati against Rana Pratap of Mewar in 1576.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Nabarun' is of Hindu origin, meaning 'new run'. In the modern context, it is most notably associated with the renowned Bengali poet and writer, Nabarun Bhattacharya. His works, which often address social issues and the human condition, have gained widespread popularity and critical acclaim. Nabarun's poetry is widely available on Goodreads, the leading platform for book discovery and reader reviews. His works are also frequently discussed and shared on Facebook. Additionally, there are several YouTube channels dedicated to reciting and analyzing his poetry, which has helped to introduce his work to a new generation of readers and audiences.

name_in_real_life.story: Krishna Nabarun, a teacher in Delhi, India, shares that their name Nabarun meaning "Night Runner" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
